title: Speech Technology
standfirst: How machines recognise and synthesise speech — signal processing, HMMs, and modern neural approaches.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the fundamentals of speech and speech technologies, their real-world applications, and provides hands-on experience with relevant speech processing toolkits. This course is also offered as an elective for PG-diploma students.
faculty: Prof. S. Umesh, Department of Electrical Engineering, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Introduction to speech and signal processing; fundamentals of sampling, Fourier analysis, and speech production and perception.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Speech analysis techniques; perceptual features, filtering, and feature extraction including MFCCs.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Statistical modeling for speech; Gaussian models, classification, and mixture models.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Vector quantization and sequence modeling; Markov chains and the Viterbi algorithm.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Hidden Markov Models (HMMs); sequence inference and probabilistic modeling.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Speech recognition systems; feature extraction and HMM-GMM based approaches.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Language modeling and introduction to neural networks; n-grams and deep learning basics.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Feedforward neural networks and training; backpropagation and introduction to CTC.

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: Recurrent neural networks and sequence modeling; applications and limitations.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Advanced neural architectures; word embeddings, sequence-to-sequence models, and convolutional neural networks.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: Transformers and modern deep learning approaches; self-attention and self-supervised learning.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: Speech synthesis and speaker recognition; end-to-end systems, verification, and diarization.
